model: Universal-inference split likelihood ratio E_n(theta) = prod over validation observations of p_{theta_hat_n}(X_i)/p_theta(X_i), with theta_hat_n fitted on a separate training stream, recomputed after every new pair of observations, with the fixed-threshold set C_n = {theta: log E_n(theta) < log(1/epsilon)} (the split-naive sequence of Pace, Salvan and Sartori, 2023, Section 3).

definitions.asymptotic persistence: lim_n P(theta in C_m for every m >= n)
definitions.Q_n: log E_n(theta) at the true parameter

claims.statement: In any model, with any permutation-symmetric training estimator, the split-naive sequence of Pace et al. (recomputed split likelihood-ratio set with fixed threshold log(1/epsilon)) has asymptotic persistence 0 whenever its single-time non-coverage does not tend to zero. Hence the conjecture of Pace, Salvan and Sartori (2023, Section 3) is false.
claims.scope: Their equation (6), definition (1.1) of asymptotic persistence and two-stream sampling scheme; Hewitt-Savage zero-one law.

claims.statement: Gaussian two-stream scheme with known variance and training mean: Q_n = log E_n(theta) = (S_n T_n - T_n^2/2)/n exactly; limsup Q_n / log log n = (sqrt5 - 1)/2 and liminf = -(sqrt5 + 1)/2 almost surely; for every epsilon and n_0 the persistence from n_0 is 0, and the tail intersection of the sets is empty almost surely.
claims.evidence: written proof in split_likelihood_persistence.pdf; script checks listed in VERIFICATION.md

claims.statement: Under regularity conditions (R1)-(R3), limsup log E_n(theta_0) / log log n = ((sqrt5 - 1)/2) mu_max(H^-1 J) almost surely; under correct specification (R4, J = H) the constant is (sqrt5 - 1)/2 in every fixed dimension.
claims.scope: Regular parametric models of fixed dimension; working likelihoods covered by the sandwich constant.
claims.evidence: written proof in split_likelihood_persistence.pdf; script checks listed in VERIFICATION.md

claims.statement: A fixed validation-to-training ratio r gives the constant c(r) = (sqrt(r^2 + 4r) - r)/2 in (0, 1); no fixed split fraction restores (1.1).
claims.scope: Gaussian model and every model satisfying (R1)-(R4).
claims.evidence: written proof in split_likelihood_persistence.pdf; script checks listed in VERIFICATION.md

claims.statement: Fixed-K cross-fitting: weighted power means with p > 0 give c(1/(K-1)); the weighted geometric mean gives 2 lambda_max(sum_j w_j A_j), equal to 1/K for equal weights; p < 0 and the minimum give 1/K; every symmetric e-merging function has constant at most c(1/(K-1)), and any e-merging function dominating a positive multiple of the minimum has constant at least 1/K, hence zero persistence.
claims.scope: Fixed number of folds with a fixed assignment; the trivial merging function F = 1 has persistence 1 and no power.
claims.evidence: written proof in split_likelihood_persistence.pdf; script checks listed in VERIFICATION.md

claims.statement: If g is a valid boundary for a scalar standard Gaussian random walk at level alpha, the threshold b(n) = lambda_1 g(n)^2 / n with lambda_1 = (sqrt5 - 1)/4 gives a (1 - alpha) confidence sequence from the split statistic.
claims.scope: Gaussian two-stream scheme, or data whose standardised increments are jointly conditionally sub-Gaussian with the Gaussian working likelihood.
claims.evidence: written proof in split_likelihood_persistence.pdf; script checks listed in VERIFICATION.md

claims.statement: Thresholds lambda_1{2 log log n + kappa log log log n + O(1)} give a valid confidence sequence at some level below 1 if and only if kappa > 3.

Checkpoint repair: with checkpoints n_k and weights w_k summing to at most 1, the set built from the fixed-n e-value at the last checkpoint with threshold 1/(alpha w_k) is a (1 - alpha) confidence sequence in every model.
claims.scope: Any model with fixed-n e-values; dominated by the Ramdas-Wang time-mixture e-process.
claims.evidence: written proof in split_likelihood_persistence.pdf; script checks listed in VERIFICATION.md

claims.statement: The finite-horizon uncoverage over n_min <= n <= R n_min converges, as n_min grows, to the probability that a stationary two-dimensional Ornstein-Uhlenbeck quadratic form exceeds log(1/epsilon) within time log R.
claims.scope: Gaussian scheme; the limit depends only on the horizon ratio R.
claims.evidence: written proof in split_likelihood_persistence.pdf; script checks listed in VERIFICATION.md
